## Archive: CURRENT-TRUTH compaction (s5512, 2026-10-18)

Verbatim material removed from docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md; git history also has it.

### Old headline M4 revisit narrative (s5321-s5395)

The current bounded work is a parked-boundary revisit. Sessions 5321 and 5325
confirm that the qualified port's transient M4 `0x8000` state appears in
stages 10/11 and is absent in stages 12/13 and task end, but the stage hooks
are not comparable to the retail instruction-PC samples. The M4 discriminator
is therefore unevaluable without a complete task-keyed sampler at a shared
boundary; no accumulator mitigation follows. Session 5325 validated the
retail oracle's whole-RDRAM positive control and recorded the exact shared-
boundary design in `docs/REVISIT-S5325-M4-SHARED-BOUNDARY-DESIGN.md`.
Session 5326 made the cxd4 sampler stride configurable and added generated
Factor 5 PCs to the port hooks; both sampler controls were live, but neither
driven arm reached the target hangar phase, so that attempt selected H3. Session
5329's missing boundary was caused by its window-key schedule, not a missing
capability. Session 5330 used the source-documented in-process autopilot route
(`3:start,6:start,9:start,12:start,16:a,20:a,24:start,28:a`) with the
validated LLE route. The rebuilt port passed the phase control at
1024/`0x00790400` and reached the required shared 512 boundary at
`0x006AB400` in 23.8 seconds; the M4 gate emitted 464 records. The M4
task-keyed comparison is resumed, but no accumulator conclusion is drawn
until the cxd4 and port tables join at that boundary.

Session 5395 added null guards at both host-facing RSP task entrypoints:
`rs64_run_lle_gfx` now returns `-1` for a null task and `get_rsp_microcode`
returns the existing unknown-task stub. The normal Debug target builds. This
is a host callback-contract guard, not evidence of a guest writer or a route
defect; no runtime null reach was observed because the available SDL verifier
failed to start the child route (`rc=126`, no SDL_QUIT line).
Session 5331 ran that comparison attempt. The oracle whole-RDRAM/VI controls
passed, and the port again reached `0x006AB400`/512, but the port output
exposed only aggregate M4 counts; it lacked actual RSP-PC, task-serial, and
step-bucket keys. H3 remained selected at that point.
Session 5332 added a regeneration-surviving key path. In the phase-gated port
run, the same-run hook control fired and 4,091 target rows carried nonzero
task serial `961`, generated PCs `0x112C`/`0x17F0`, and increasing per-task
step values at `0x006AB400`/512. The task serial did not vary because the
target was one long graphics task, so this proves field availability and
rules out H3, but does not yet select H1/H2 or authorize a mitigation.
Session 5335 ran the corrected cxd4 retail arm and the port arm with same-run
positive controls. Retail produced 10,000 whole-RDRAM hits, live VI controls,
2,091 graphics task joins, and 1,215 tasks with transient `-32768` VACC lanes;
the port produced 4,096 target rows. The exact join remained unavailable:
retail PCs were `0x0088..0x0FE8`, while port rows used `0x112C`/`0x17F0`, and
the phase origins were `0x006AB800` versus `0x006AB400`. H3 is selected for
this discriminator; no writer or mitigation follows. See
`docs/REVISIT-S5335-M4-COMPARISON.md`.

ROGUESQ_FORCE_SEL knob built; arms s5505_sel_log/f2/f7 queued; fold from SOAK-RESULTS (control = `[level] sel@B40` lines). See PORTING-STATE s5505.

### M6 mission-outcome machinery (static, single-source unless noted)

- Byte 0x80130B14 = mainGameLoop result code. Loop at 0x8003E304 runs
  cinematicLoopBody until bit 0x100 of 0x80130B50 is set, then 0x8003E3C4
  switches on B14 via table 0x8003A3E8: 1 = level complete (0x8003E3E4), 2 =
  lose a life (0x8003E4BC), 3/4/5 -> 0x8003E514/E544 (s5610).
- 800C7738 / 800C776C are flag-setters (bit 0x4 / 0x8 of flagword 0x8010C9E0
  if gate 0x8010CA20==0). In lv0_checkComplexObjectives get(2)>=3 and
  get(3)>=9 call 7738 (event 2 -> gate 4 -> Mode2 -> B14=2, LOSE); only
  get(10)>=6 (0x80138084) calls 776C (event 3 -> gate 3 -> Mode1 -> B14=1 WIN)
  (s5612; supersedes s5604-s5611 "gate-4 = win"). Gate 6 = 800FADEC per-player
  respawn. Switch 800FA858, subphase byte 0x8010C9F0, timer float 0x8010C9EC.
  Loss counter 0x80138064 = gObjectiveCounts[1]; gObjectiveBooleans
  0x801388A0; mask 0x130B15 is HUD-only.
- Test hooks in main.cpp: `ROGUESQ_MISSION_WIN` (lose-arm poke),
  `ROGUESQ_MISSION_WIN_REAL=1` (get(10)=6; s5612 one win B14=1 then 0/4 repro,
  get(1..9)=0, get(10)=6-7, gate g5->g0->g4(b14=2)->g6),
  `ROGUESQ_MISSION_WIN_NOPOKE=1` (control: g4/b14=2 tail appears unpoked, s5616).
- hudbit chain (s5617-s5623, PARKED): only callers of setHudEnableBit4/8 are

  lv2_checkComplexObjectives sets bit4 only when getObjectiveBoolean(0x64 or
  0x6D)==1. `ROGUESQ_LOG_HUDBIT=1` logs `[hudbit]`, `[cco]` and
  setObjectiveBoolean (0x800C7540) id/val (`tools/apply_s5618_hudbit_log.py`,

- **s5799 projectile-direction block: live and not stale (initial runtime

  words matched their last-writer table and the positive `[recw]`/`[recv]`
  controls fired. P words are written through the

  substructure, while direction words come from its cross/normalize and
  perpendicular-jitter intermediates. The runtime probe did not expose the
  upstream subtraction; s5800's static trace found it in the caller. The
  runtime source still establishes live, non-stale writes, while H8b is now
  selected by the combined static/runtime evidence.
- **s5801 projectile-direction upstream source: object/mesh-derived input
  exists.** Static generated-code trace shows `spawnProbeDroidGroundImpactEffect`
  calls `getObjectMeshTransformOrLocal`, which resolves an active NPC/object
  slot and copies or world-transforms a mesh record; the caller subtracts the
  droid position and forms normalized cross-product axes before calling
  `generatePerpEmitDirectionWithJitter`. This preserves H8b over H8a/H8c but
  is single-source static evidence; target versus attachment semantics remain
  open.

- **s5802 object/mesh path classified.** `getObjectMeshTransformOrLocal` masks
  the caller object's `+0x130` key, walks the active-NPC slot chain at
  `0x80130BB0`, and resolves an NPC context. With a non-null context `+0xC`
  mesh record it copies context `+0x8` and calls `transformMeshPartIntoWorld`,
  whose matrix/vector fields produce the returned world position. This selects
  H10b (an active object's mesh attachment/local transform) over H10c (a
  generic effect asset); target-object versus firing-object semantics remain
  open because the indirect caller supplying the object was not recovered.
  Single-source static evidence.

- **s5803 object provenance classified.** The spawn routine is not called with
  a target argument. `triggerCueWithSlotEffect` dispatches through
  `slotDispatcherIter`; the dispatcher loads a slot node from the effect table,
  passes the node as handler `a0`, and calls the node's function pointer at
  `slot+0`. `spawnProbeDroidGroundImpactEffect` then reads `slot+4` as its
  object and passes that object's `+0x38` to `getObjectMeshTransformOrLocal`.
  This selects H10b (the firing/effect object's active mesh attachment/local
  transform) over H10a (a selected target supplied as the indirect argument)
  and H10c (a generic asset with no active-object identity). Static evidence is
  single-source; the next G1 unit is real-input mission progression/win.

   levels 11..18 from the repaired queue.
4. Sweep remaining levels for route+hold, then add framebuffer and forced-hit
   objective checks to every level.
5. Fold the human lv0 play when available; a loss, softlock, or broken render is
   a new root-cause datum, while a win establishes a tooling limitation.
6. After G1 coverage, pursue G3 render fidelity and any distinct G4 crash/stall
   datum. G2 owner listening remains the audio-fidelity follow-up.
7. Optional: qualify a fresh MIPS source-to-ELF patch after higher-priority G1.

## s6129 update (G1d 21:9 heap root cause)
The 21:9 heap deficit is the widened framebuffer carve: partitionFramebufferMemory (0x80000DD4) places fbs at the top of the 8 MB (globals 0x801163D8/DC/E4/F8), each w*448*2 (512: 0x70000; 1045: 0xE4980), so 21:9 moves heap end -0x74980, fb base and the top-down pool -0xE9300 and costs ~1.9 MB of the 2.6 MB 4:3 free space (-> NULL rs_malloc(0x1000), s6127). The 0x2DB000/0x3E4B00 "block" is that pool region. 16:9 (796) has no heap NULL but stalls in initMission -> initializeObjectiveTracking -> lv1_initializeObjectTracking (new, uncharacterized). Fix routes: lift RT64's 8 MB rdram cap (osMemSize up to 16 MB; ROGUESQ_OSMEM_MB clamps to 8 in recomp.cpp:565) or shrink the carve. NEXT: find where RT64 caps rdram, and charcterize the 16:9 stall.

### G1c span-filter chain, settled facts (s6476-s6528)

- Missing dd>=4 ground is cells rejected by the per-cell span filter in `streamTerrainGridCellsByDistance` (stream returns empty on 15-20% of dd4 calls vs ~0.3% dd1, s6492/s6493), not fog (s6486), not DL-chunk/pool/grid caps (s6414, s6416, s6487), not the LOD index (0x80137CE4 = difficulty, s6485), not distance gates (s6483/s6484).
- Span grid `0x80130DB0..0x80132DAF` is a real 64x64, 8192-byte grid, fully written (s6510-s6512, s6521). Writers: 0x800426D8, 0x80042820, 0x80042A74/78, 0x80042DB4, 0x80042DC0 (the filter's own `0x7F` stamp after reading); 0x80042EBC/EC4 never fire.
- Consumer 0x80042D50: skip if A==B==-128; reject if A<rec[3] or rec[4]<B (signed lb). dd4 drives the edge loop to x>=32 ~620x more than dd1 and 58% saturate at -128, colliding with the empty sentinel; both compares fire on dd4 EMPTY (s6515, s6521-s6526). The -128 clamp itself is irrelevant (s6527).
- Table base `[hdr+0x1C]` is set by `load_level_hmp` (0x80043E64) per level load; mission table 802EE7B4 is EMPTY 0/2643 at dd1 vs 345/2402 at dd4 (s6517-s6518).
- Same-run SPANFORCE toggle: terrain tight 0.047 off vs 0.209 force (H-rejects-hide-terrain, s6528); accept-all costs ~2.3x sd_wall (126.8 vs 54.6 ms/task, s6536). Saturation writer still unnamed.
- `[ddclamp]` (s6548): lvl1 terrain is 64x64 with a 2048-cell cap at 0x80130C4C; dd4 footprint ~88x137 and dd6 ~101x174 both clamp to terrain, so dd6 cannot draw more on lvl1.

### G3c / G1d / G1e closure facts (s6378-s6546)

- G3c(a) far-edge: no opt-in rougher than retail (stair_med s6449, s6544); height-byte fade null; dd2 holes were the 16384 ucode cap (s6403-s6405). Closed no-regression.
- G3c(b) spike wedges: FD57 VU chain replays exactly (s6379/s6385) and independent cxd4 scalar replay agrees (s6388); angrylion replay lights the same 16/79 wedges as the RDP model (s6441, s6454) -> H-hw-draws, retail-faithful. `ROGUESQ_CULL_SPIKE` stays opt-in; owner to decide default-on. Reference notes: `docs/G3C-SPIKE-REFERENCE.md`.
- G3c(c) turning shake: arm-independent jerk (s6455) and identical spin/NOSPIN wall-dt (s6458) -> retail 30 fps judder; [g3c] VI stamps arrive in task-completion bursts.
- G1d: 16:9 (796x448) and 21:9 (1024x448) flight fill the frame with HUD at edges, logo centred after the 320-wide cam fix (s6427-s6430); hangar rows 436-448/448 lit (s6438); wide-aspect holes not the ucode cap (s6437); wide flight origin is allocator-dependent, never gate on a fixed origin (s6393). M3 safety: `rs64_run_lle_gfx` rejects null RDRAM/DMEM/task (s6392).
- G1e: retail ~30 fps vs FPS60 ~59 (0x8011A8F4, s6256-s6257); md5/per-VI period approach abandoned (s6452).

Session 6506 replaced the invalid cross-function cumulative join with an
invocation-local writer baseline and atomic key in the existing s650 fixup
path. The Debug build passed. The prescribed pinned dd1/dd4 run produced 14
dd1 and 8 dd4 `[postring]` rows, including nonempty and EMPTY controls; every
row had `key==seq`, positive writer activity, and nonnegative interval deltas.
The first dd1 interval was `144,144,0,0`; subsequent dd1 rows were `6..9,6..9,0,0`,
while dd4 rows were `49..53,49..53,0,0`. This removes the unsigned-underflow
join defect and shows the observed interval activity is at DB4/DC0, not EBC/EC4.
The result identifies the boundary/race artifact but does not yet prove which
writer changed the post-bin table; no game behavior or default changed.

Session 6508 added a regeneration-safe per-site byte mask and post-table diff
to that keyed probe. The Debug build passed. The pinned run held both dd1 and
dd4 for 151 s with zero VI stalls/crash markers; dd1 produced 14 keyed rows
and dd4 108, including nonempty and EMPTY controls. On the initial matching
controls, dd1 changed byte mask 0x80 with interval mask DC0=0x80, then 0x03
with DC0=0x03; dd4 changed 0x800000 then 0x18 with DC0 matching those masks.
DB4, EBC, and EC4 interval masks were zero in those controls. This selects
the concrete 0x80042DC0 writer for the observed post-bin change in two
independent arms. Later rows retain a nonzero diff with zero new interval
mask, so this does not claim every later mutation is DC0. No mitigation or
default changed.

Session 6509 classified the selected DC0 writer's live target/value in the same
keyed probe. The regeneration-safe instrument passed a Debug build. Clean
per-attempt evidence supplied dd1 with 14 keyed rows (6 EMPTY, 8 nonempty) and
dd4 with 31 keyed rows (23 EMPTY, 8 nonempty), with zero `[CRASH]` markers;
the positive controls therefore passed. Every sampled DC0 store wrote `0x7F`.
Both arms produced targets outside the 24-byte span table
`0x80130DB0..0x80130DC7`; dd4 labels these `span_mode=active_accept`, meaning
the existing draw-distance bound accepted addresses beyond the table, while
dd1 labels the bound `disabled`. This selects H-DC0-corrupt over
H-DC0-legitimate: the writer is `streamTerrainGridCellsByDistance` at
`0x80042DC0`, and its `ctx->r21` target path is the next upstream boundary to
audit. No guard or gameplay behavior changed.

Session 6510 reconstructed that target path in one paired pinned run. The
regeneration-safe probe logged 512 DC0 rows in each arm; dd1 had 15 keyed
postring rows and dd4 had 8, with the existing nonempty/EMPTY controls, zero
crash markers, and zero 30-second VI stalls. Every sampled row reconstructed
`addr` exactly as `r5 + r14`, where `r5 = r20 + (r30 << 6)` and `r14 =
0x80130DB0`; `r3` was always `0x7F`. The base is an offset into the 64-byte
row grid, not a host pointer, and the OUT addresses are the expected
row/inner positions beyond the first 24 bytes. This selects H-coherent-stream
over H-corrupt-input and overturns s6509's 24-byte-table interpretation: the
span table is the larger grid already admitted by the `0x2000` bound. No guard,
game behavior, or default changed.

Session 6511 completed the full-grid discriminator in one paired pinned run.
The regenerated probe passed its positive controls with 14 keyed dd1 rows and
8 keyed dd4 rows, no crash/abort markers, and no observed VI stall. Every row
reported a 64x64, 8192-byte span grid with non-127 contents. Full-range writer
activity was observed from DB4 and DC0 in both arms; dd1 addresses began near
`0x80130DB0` and dd4 addresses reached the outer grid, while EBC/EC4 had no
full-grid writes in the sampled rows. This refutes H-short-init (only the first
24 bytes initialized) and supports H-full-grid: the DC0 stream writes are
coherent accesses into a real 64x64 grid, not stale bytes outside a 24-byte
table. It does not yet prove whether the dd4 EMPTY result is a legitimate
span-table filter outcome or identify any initialization writer outside the
four instrumented sites. No guard, game behavior, or default changed.

Session 6512 extended the probe to eight distinct span-store PCs and added a

held dd1 and dd4 for 151 seconds, with 14 and 108 keyed rows respectively,
zero crash markers, and zero 30-second VI stalls. The `[span-base]` positive
control fired in both arms; every sampled baseline/return snapshot was a full
64x64, 8192-byte grid. The eight-site table showed activity only at
`0x800426D8`, `0x80042820`, `0x80042A74`, `0x80042A78`, `0x80042DB4`, and
`0x80042DC0`; `0x80042EBC` and `0x80042EC4` remained zero. The dd1 EMPTY
control had interval DB4/DC0 deltas `6,6`; the dd4 EMPTY control had `49,49`,
while its selected 24-byte table was all `127`. This rules out the two
unobserved EBC/EC4 sites as the source and makes an uninstrumented initializer
less likely, but does not yet select legitimate filter input over a late
DB4/DC0 rewrite. No guard, gameplay behavior, or default changed.

Session 6514 selected H-late-rewrite. The keyed probe read the span bytes
before the `0x7F` stores. Both pinned arms held 151 s with zero stalls and
zero crash lines; `[span-base]` fired, and nonempty rows had `npass>0` while
every EMPTY row had `npass==0`. dd1 EMPTY was 6/6 late-rewrite (`nother` 6-7);
dd4 EMPTY was 100/100 (`nother` 33-68). Sampled populated cells were 127 at
return, and the DB4 interval delta matched DC0 and `nclear`. Rasterizer census
counts were already nonzero, so H-missing-source is refuted; zero EMPTY rows
were all-sentinel, so H-filter-legitimate is refuted. The stamp is the
filter's own `0x7F` immediate. dd4's first populated sample had second-plane
byte 127 on 100/100 EMPTY rows; dd1's had 25 on 6/6. No guard or default changed.

Session 6515 counted the two compares on that same keyed return. Both pinned
arms held 151 s with zero stalls and zero crash lines; `[span-base]` fired,
nonempty rows had `npass>0`, and `ns0+ns1+npass+nskip==nd` on every row.
dd4 EMPTY was 100/100 both predicates (s1 is 42-64% of clears, median 57%,
and every s1 clear is cell+4 < plane 127). Sampled s0 operands there are
span -128 < cell+3 -38; sampled s1 operands are cell+4 about -38 < plane 127.
dd1 EMPTY was 6/6 s0-only (span 38-41 < cell+3 109, ns1=0), and both arms'
nonempty returns were s0-only too. This selects H-both and refutes a
single-predicate account. No guard or default changed.

- **s6716 G1e dd4 CEILING (bridge is essential work).** xctrace Time Profiler, lvl5 FPS60 dd4 PROBES=0, 15 s dense flight,
  lines via lldb (tools/xctrace_tp.py): Gfx thread 4259 samples = factor5_ucode self 76% (LLE interpreter) + bridge 18.4%.

- **s6705 G1e: ROGUESQ_RDP_ASYNC=1 (opt-in) runs RT64 RDP processing on a worker thread** (command words copied at submit,
  drained before dp_complete/present). Same-run toggle, lvl5 FPS60 dd2: 11.70 -> 10.46 ms/task, 49.3 -> 54.9 tasks/s, 301 s
  clean, frames sane (docs/img/g1e_s6705_async_sheet.png). Short of 60: only ~1.2 of the ~5 ms RT64 share overlaps. Default off.
  s6706 split (same recipe, [g1e-aq], tools/g1e_aq.py): H-endload. The defer layer releases a task's RDP ranges only at ring laps
  (unmerged, ~9.5k calls) and at ucode exit; that final ~120 kB commit is 3.4-3.5 of the worker's 4.2 ms and cannot overlap the
  RSP. Producer copy/mutex adds ~0.9 ms. Net same-run gain 0.7 ms/task (s6705 measured 1.2).
  **s6707 refines H-endload: the tail is a fixed ~3.3 ms, not bytes.** Streaming the deferred list every 16 kB
  (ROGUESQ_RDP_STREAM_KB, default 16 with async; same-run ROGUESQ_RDP_STREAM_TOGGLE) shrank the last job 150 -> 7.7 kB and
  RT64 calls 8.9k -> 0.6k per task, but last-job time stayed 3.26 -> 3.29 ms and drain 3.28 -> 3.33 ms (total 9.36 vs 9.13,
  noise). So ~3.3 ms is spent in what the final range triggers (fullSync: flush/submitFramebufferPair/workload), not in
  parsing. **s6708: fullSync = fb-pair render** (fsRender 3.0 of 3.2 ms: ~1.7 ms CPU encode, 1.3 ms GPU execute/wait;
  flush/submitFb/upload ~0; tools/g1e_fs.py, segments sum to total). **ROGUESQ_RDP_NODRAIN=1** (with ROGUESQ_RDP_ASYNC=1)
  skips the task-end drain so the next task's RSP overlaps it (present/sync submits still drain). Same-run lvl5 FPS60 dd2:
  Gfx ms/task 10.18 sync / 8.88 drained / 4.54 no-drain, tasks/s 50.1 / 57.8 / 59.9, frames sane
  (docs/img/g1e_s6708_nodrain_sheet.png). **s6709 qualified** (ASYNC=1 NODRAIN=1, FPS60, 300 s): lvl1 dd1 / lvl10 dd4 / lvl5 dd4
  0 crash, 0 stall, frames sane; lvl1/lvl10 59.5 tasks/s; same-run lvl5 dd4 Gfx 9.56 -> 5.16 ms, 51.6 -> 55.9 tasks/s (p10
  30 -> 42), worker keeps up (pend_jobs 2.0). In OWNER-OPT-INS (default off). Remaining dd4 gap is not the Gfx thread.
  **s6710: the dd4 gap is the game's serial frame loop (H-serial).** [g1b-gt] (ROGUESQ_G1B=1: per guest thread CPU ms + ms
  blocked in osRecvMesg; control: every slot's cpu+blk+rest ~1000 ms/s) + s4911 queue table (ROGUESQ_S4908=1), tools/g1e_gt.py.
  Game thread = OSId 3 (slot 8), the only real guest CPU: 0.29-0.42 s/s, so not saturated (H-guest refuted as sole cause);
  audio SP queue wait 0.01 ms (H-audio-rsp refuted). Its blocked time is submitGfxFrame waiting for its own just-kicked gfx
  task (mq 0x8011A7E8, as=3 fast 151 / slow 345 ms/s) plus waitForPostSwapAck for the VI (0x80128CF0, 420-550 ms/s).
  Per second, (cpu + gfx wait)/frame vs tasks/s r=-0.63 (139 s): <10 ms -> 55.7/s, 10-14 -> ~44, >18 -> 38.5. Two runs
  (osid-keyed and slot-keyed builds) agree. The game itself has no CPU/RSP overlap, so 60 needs cpu+gfx per frame < ~10 ms.
  **s6711 per-frame timeline (ROGUESQ_G1E_TL=<file>, tools/g1e_tl.py) refines this to H-rsp.** spTaskSchedulerThread
  kicks the queued gfx task at VI+0.2 ms; the game's ~3.7 ms run overlaps it; the frame makes its VI iff the gfx task
  (Gfx start -> RSP exit) is < ~14 ms: P(miss) 0.17 at 12-14 ms, 0.56 at 14-16, 0.88 above. Slow camera phase (~8 s
  autopilot cycle facing dense dd4 terrain): 13.2 ms/task, 789 kB RDP out vs 4.6 ms / 267 kB fast; 17 us per kB in both.
  Handoff latencies < 1 ms, guest run 3.7-5.5 ms (not the term). The s6710 "~10 ms" was a per-second blend (superseded).
  **s6712 split of that task (ROGUESQ_G1E_AQ=1 -> [g1e-split] per s; `sample` profiles): H-interp.** Task cost is linear in
  RDP commands (DPC_END bumps, up to ~50k/task dense): owner-play config (no recipe logging) ~0.6 ms + 257 ns/cmd interp side
  + 55 ns/cmd bridge (half of that is the timer itself); commit ~0.01 ms. Recipe logging arm: same slope (328 vs 321 ns/cmd
  pre-fix), so H-log refuted. Positive control: 2 us spin per submit in alternate 10 s windows lands in submit_ms (45k calls
  -> +91 ms). Profile without instrument terms: LLE interpreter (factor5_ucode + RSP:: vector ops + byte-wise
  dma_rdram_to_dmem) ~70%, bridge ~10%, in-ucode probes ~10%. Fixed: [m4-y8000] was default-ON (summary+fflush ~600/s,
  2/3 of the log volume); now opt-in (ROGUESQ_LOG_M4_Y8000=1): dense task 11.98 -> 11.74 ms at ~35k cmds, log 104 -> 45 MB.

- s6653 "level 18 has visual evidence but no numeric terrain acceptance" (s6654: the bounded bright low-chroma snow arm accepts both flight views while every control holds). Believable because their rel 0.046/0.068 is below the original 0.08 floor; that band remains unchanged.
- s6651 "level 17 does not pass the frozen rule, and the grey trench box is not a sky arm" (s6652: neutral8 ≥ 0.80 inside luma [38, 55] with |channel means| ≤ 8 accepts n=2300, 1/10; canon_bad 0; mission 11/13; both title skies stay false; m3150 stays a sky miss at neutral8 0.613). Believable because dark ≥ 0.60, the blue arm, the orange arm and the tan-cloud arm all miss luma 42.5 with R−G 1.4, and the top 4% of that frame is the same grey, so lowering dark does not accept the chase.

- s6643 "level 10 is a flight and the frozen rule rejects the sky 0/12" (s6644: tan-cloud arm accepts 11/12; n=2900 stays a craft miss at edge 0.013; title sky stays false because G−B is ~5 while the clouds are ≥22; canon_bad 0; mission 11/13). Believable because the route key is 0x690400 and EVERY=50 phase-locked onto one of the two buffers.
- s6631 first cut "any block with next > e4 is the tail, so walking until then caps the arena" (same session, did=3 at a header exactly equal to e4). Believable because s6630 described the free block as covering [e4, top) and the header as e4-0x10. The punch's reserved size ends on e4, so the free header is e4 and the old walker returned before cutting.
- s6630's first classifier label "H-stale-target, because inflateEnd frees the zlib window before the depth upload" (same session, H-live-overlap). Believable because that free is real and precedes the read. It does not move `801163E4`, which still names `0x80B56000` at malloc, free, SETZIMG and the upload.
- s6629 "why the zlib window overlaps the depth image is open" (s6630: the image was still reserved when `rs_malloc` returned inside it; s6631 then stopped that heap at the depth pointer). Believable because s6629 named only the store. At s6630 heap `8010FEFC` still ran through to RAM top; heap `8010FF18` already stopped at the depth pointer.
- s6628 "writer between A/B unknown" is resolved at the watched word by s6629 exact pre/post stores and caller context: rs_zcalloc clears a zlib window there. The earlier witness lacked store hooks. s6630 resolves the ownership class; it does not make the whole stripe one 32 KB zero.
- s6628 closes H-swap/H-alias for the measured upload (single-source): believable because the earlier native witness preceded byteswapping and did not record the live mapping. Post-swap and exit preserve `0x9EC4`, and both sites use the identical host address; the zero appears between them.
- s6627 closes "the 1024x447 `copyToRAM` at `0x00B20000` writes the `0x0000` stripe" (it covers `0x00BB0020`). Believable because that span contains every stripe address and the same write's own image y=180 is rawBe 0. Refuted: the absolute sample is rawBe `0x9F4C` on all 935 covering writebacks, the call count does not move, and the upload still reads `0x0000`. The image-y zero is phys `0x00B7A020`.
- s6626 closes "fbChangesDrawDepth, its boolean mask, or its viewport manufactures the 21:9 depth stripe from a clear or smooth guest field" (H-upload). Believable because the GPU image goes from a read-back clear of 1.0 to the stripe inside copyFromChanges, and a discard mask cannot paint 0 by itself. Refuted: the guest words already are the stripe and match the GPU on 142/142 samples (mae 0), shader endian, site state.cpp:2604.
- s6625 "after the zero head, x=16 is a smooth 0.964..0.961 ramp and x=1007 stays 1.0". Believable because x=16 does contain 0.96408 and x=1007 has more exact-1 samples (31 vs 13). Both columns actually interleave ~0.96 and 1.0. The stable part is the exact-0 head.
- s6625 closes "the 21:9 zeros are unwritten depth tiles (create-clear never applied, so a readback of 0)". Believable because Metal does not clear a D32 texture at creation, and a different 1024x480 target's first sample in the same run was exact 0. Refuted on the floor texture: clearDepthTarget read back 1.0 on both columns, and the following copyFromChanges replaced those pixels.
- s6623 "shader-to-attachment MAE 37 at 21:9 means the first wrong stage is an attachment write after a sane shader" (s6624: the same shader color is stored at 16:9, where depth is 1.0 and LESS passes, and rejected at 21:9, where a nearer striped depth already occupies the columns). Believable because the UAV record is written before the depth test and matched the 16:9 attachment exactly.
- s6614 lead "dtdx*x at the outer third diverges on 21:9" (s6615: dtdx shrinks by about 796/1024 and the texel matches to about 0.05). Believable because the sample x grows with the framebuffer and s6613 only cancelled that product at x=0.
- s6612 "21:9 S at the left edge walks off the 64-wide mask while 16:9 stays inside" (s6613: 0/16 pairs do that; S at x=0 matches). Believable because the x span and dsdx scale with width. x_major moves the other way and the product cancels.
- s6610 ring-only "second=fbw-512 fixes the 16:9 radar" (the ring reached the retail inset, but the wedge stayed at 769..792 with 0 pixels inside the ring). Believable because s6609's red-ring edge equalled retail+second. The disc is a separate pre-shift `ROGUESQ_SHIFT_REGION` writer; shift must be A, not RA.

  fingerprint checks columns 269..335 in 336 rows; visible bottom garbage is

### Headline bullets: wide/dd span fixes and the present thread (s6879-s6891)

- **FIXED s6879-s6880: wide flight lost far terrain, then 21:9 crashed.** ROGUESQ_G1D_FPDEPTH (default on, =0 old) undoes our s6144 forward-reach loss. That exposed a 21:9 crash: scanConvertTriangleToSpanTable (0x80042820) overran the span tables into the descriptor at dd 1, because the s6049 bound was gated on dd != 1. ROGUESQ_G1D_SPANBOUND (default on, =0 old) covers wide frames; k=1 retail. Same binary: =0 crashes, default holds lvl1 21:9 302 s, lvl5/lvl10 135 s; 4:3 and 16:9 0 px changed vs before the bound. 21:9 look is single-source; sheets docs/owner_sheet_s6879_wide_depth.png, docs/owner_sheet_s6880_219_depth.png.
- **s6881: s6879/s6880 now replay from pristine; wide + dd same-pose frames exist.** Regen stopped on an inline s6879 call that ran before the s6144 text exists; call removed, RS64_REPLAY runs it. Compare 2684/82/17/1 = s6871, s6879/s6880/s6049 text in funcs_9 identical to live. New apply scripts go in RS64_REPLAY only (docs/REGEN-VERIFY.md). No regen binary linked or run. Test-only fix: POSE_LOCK and POSE_FREEZE rejected player pointers above 8 MB, and wide + dd spills the player (0x809A6350), so keys were never zeroed and no freeze fired. 16:9 dd4 vs 4:3 dd4 now at identical pose: mad 11.53/11.54/17.53, ctl 25.95/24.00/66.16. Sheet docs/owner_sheet_s6881_wide_dd4.png.

- **FIXED s6882: wide + dd flight ran at 6-9 game fps at 21:9 dd4 and 11-20 at 16:9 dd4 (non-FPS60 recipe); now 20-31 at both.** ORIGIN: the span fill loops in scanConvertTriangleToSpanTable took x bounds of 0x7F7F, the span fill's own bytes. Inference, row count not logged: edge walkers 0x80041FA4/0x80042118 write the 80-row min/max arrays with no limit, so a deep footprint reads max[i>=80] from 0x80130DB0. Each row then walked ~32k x at three float divides, every store skipped (3.84e9 skips in 130 s). Same pose: frames 0 px changed, 0 skips vs 59777 log lines. ROGUESQ_G1D_SPANNARROW (default on where the s6049/s6880 bound runs, =0 old; retail dd1 4:3 untouched). Replays from pristine. Overrun itself: see s6883.
- **FIXED s6883: span scan overrun at dd > 1 or wide; 21:9 dd4 now 30 fps not 20-22 (recipe, non-FPS60).** ORIGIN: edge walkers of scanConvertTriangleToSpanTable fill the 80-row min/max arrays unbounded (row 264 at 21:9 dd4, 136 at 4:3 dd4, 65 at 21:9 dd1), and y/x outside 0..63 passed the s6049/s6880 byte bound into the wrong row or table (9e8 stores, all 4096 cells non-empty). ROGUESQ_G1D_SPANCELL default 3 where the s6882 gate runs (=0 old; bit 1 edge rows to host arrays, 0 px and no rate change alone; bit 2 cell bound, the active term; 4 control). Same binary, repeat 0 px: lvl1 21:9 tasks p50 21 -> 30, lvl5 21 -> 30, ucode 25.7 -> 18.9; lvl10 unchanged. Pixels: <= 3.2% change, a tie vs dd1 (13.84 vs 13.68). Sim identical per tick on every pair (tickdiv, controls fire), retail 4:3 dd1 0 px. Replays from pristine. lvl10 frames pending soaks s6883_l10z/d. Sheet docs/owner_sheet_s6883_spancell.png.
- **s6884: FPS60 21:9 dd4 cost split (lvl1, pinned, same 1612 ticks, all arms 0 px).** Logging text has no measured cost (r100 = r000 at 29.6 fps; r111 = r011 at 59.7). 30 fps = RT64 inline on the Gfx thread (sd_wall 21.6 ms) plus FAST off/PROBES on, which any ROGUESQ_LOG_* env sets: F alone 30.0, A (ASYNC+NODRAIN) alone 44.1, both 59.7, repeat 58.9. Measurement recipes understate rate through FAST/PROBES, not log volume; set ROGUESQ_G1E_FAST=1 ROGUESQ_G1E_PROBES=0 when timing.

The job runs updateScreen FIFO on the RDP worker. Keyed lvl1 21:9 dd4, 2 pairs: tasks min/p10 41/46, 44/50 -> 58/60, 59/60; s below 50 11, 4 -> 0, 0. - **FIXED s6885: 21:9 flight showed frames out of order and dropped some; 4:3 never did.** ORIGIN: needStaticPresent's `screenFbSize.x >= 1024` (session 21, for the retail 1024-wide phase, which has no early presents) also matches 21:9 flight, VI width 1024. So the normal path pushed a stale-origin present behind every early present, 2 per workload, and the present thread ran whichever was last in the queue. ROGUESQ_WIDE_EARLY default on (=0 old): width counts only after 8 VIs with no early present. Same binary, lvl1 FPS60 + SCREEN_JOB, 70 s of flight, off -> on: dd1 backward steps 17.19 -> 0/s, frames never shown 8.10 -> 0.16/s; dd4 4.79 -> 0, 8.69 -> 1.11. Non-FPS60: 60 presents/s of 30 frames -> 30. Game rate unchanged, 0 crashes, no gap > 250 ms in any whole run (title and menus included). 4:3 fixed-binary arm: 0 backward, gaps match pre-fix. Frame identity is by buffer and time (W rows), not pixels; the look is unjudged, and 16:9 (VI width 768) was not run: excluded by the width test only.

- s6880 first reading "n219 k2 worse than o219 at 21:9" (hz_p90 31 vs 7.5, superseded s6880 same session). Believable because the tool had just scored 16:9 well; its 21:9 fit is bad (sx 1.22, sy 1.48) and the frames show the reverse.
- s6876 "in-place rotation writer = buildEffectObjectWorldTransform" as the pitch lead (superseded s6877). Believable because it made 8 of 10 [camcaller] rows; that was call count, it never changes word 5.
- s6875 NEXT "add a third dt to test linearity" as written, and the s6876 draft reading "dead-band settles the pitch" (superseded s6876). Believable because 1/45 looked like a third dt and the dead-band is truly per tick; dt is rounded to 1/60 ticks and the knob fires without moving the pitch.
- s6873 "FPS60 pass count follows tick rate" and "FPS60 k0/k1 not explained by frame age" (superseded s6875). Believable because the dt variants stayed near each limiter's own rate, so dt and rate never crossed, and the frame-age estimate assumed half a tick. Crossed arms: dt decides the path and camera pitch; a whole tick of presentation lag explains the rest.
- **"Pinned pose" on dd arms (s6445-s6583, superseded s6872).** POSE_PIN_POSITION never held position: the unit-range filter skips world-unit words (s6582 x ran 15..113), and even written every poll the ship flies on, because +0x4C is a per-tick copy. Believable because attitude did pin and the flag name said position. Cross-run dd figures from those arms (s6470, s6544, s6547) are attitude-only, not same-pose.
- s6268 "symbol sweep COMPLETE" and s3209/s3210 "0x80106C50 is a real callable" (superseded s6868). s6268 counted the syms toml, not the generated tree, where 30 table renames had never landed. s3209 saw a jal and took it for a caller; that site is decoded data. docs/GENERATED-NAME-CENSUS.md.
- s6004 "lvl10-15 mission_cycles=0, in flight the whole hold" (superseded s6867): mission_cycles only counts 0x690400->0x6AB400 origin changes, so it read 0 while lvl11 restarted twice and lvl14 once. Use inits= from the summary.

  match), so hold counted from t=6..31 s, not flight. Believable because alive/crash/stall all read clean and mission_t looked like a number.
  Flight actually held (tools/audit_hold_flight.py, from [initMission]): s6788/s6789 lvl5 dd4 231 s, lvl10 dd4 124 s; s6832 lvl1 229 s, lvl10 124 s;

  believable because impacts per game s were equal and every hit followed an impact. s6816: the hp hits are homing missiles,
  not bolts; the deficit is fewer turrets in range after a frame-locked terrain scrape at 15.4 s changes the player's path.

  believable because the sequence (HUD off, destruction) looked scripted and only 18 VIs were dropped. s6814: it is the
  passive player's death, later at FPS60 because fewer 50-hp hits land per game second; timers are dt-exact.

  been hiding terrain (more terrain = more cost). s6810: those arms carried census + terrain-trace logging; clean dd4 = 59.3.
- **(s6770 -> s6772)** "+0x39 bits 0x00200000 -> 16, 0x00400000 -> 17; +0x31=LEVEL selects bonus missions".
  Bits are 0x00100000/0x00200000/0x00400000 -> 16/17/18, and the game clamps +0x31 to 16 on load, so missions 18/19
  are reached only by moving the cursor. Believable because +0x31 selected missions 1-16 exactly and m17 = cursor 16.
- **(s6770 -> s6771)** "mission 17 never calls runInMissionFrame 0x800FA730; flight at 512 wide ~24 s port / ~39 s
  retail; later Start presses pause the race". The 512-wide screen at those times is the LEVEL SELECT (its hologram ticks
  0x800C6674 and calls rand from 0x800B0xxx); m17b's presses ended before the pick, so neither arm ever raced. Believable
  because the level select and the race share VI width 512 and the rand callers looked mission-like.

- **(s6070/s6403 -> s6762)** "ROGUESQ_UCODE_CAP default 16384 = retail behaviour". Hardware has no iteration cap; retail
  draws the HUD in lvl9 frames the 16384 cap truncated. Believable because no dd1 4:3 frame had been seen to fire it
  (s6070 saw 0 fires at dd0.5; the truncation was only ever reported at dd>1/wide, where 65536 was already default).

- **(s6749/s6752-s6754 -> s6755)** "port runs a flat 2.00 VI per frame" / "port update_screen 61-62/s" and the
  s6754 elapsed-VI figures: the port VI column (rs64_vi_n_g) counts update_screen, and the VI thread re-emitted 1.4%
  of VIs, so port "VI" counts were ~1.4% high before the s6755 deadline fix. Believable because update_screen is
  driven once per VI loop pass, so it looked like a VI count. Relative tick comparisons stand.

- **s6740 "the 255/248 decoder-convention idea is refuted; the 2.5% gain is 512-flight-only"** -> superseded s6744. Believable
  because the cinematic logo/snow frames showed gain ~1.00 with the same decoder; but those are textures (5-bit on both
  sides) or saturated, so they cannot show it. Shaded 3D loses the gain under v<<3 in flight and in the 640 intro.
- s6739 "retail G channel +3.6..+3.9/255 above the port, possible H-shade" (believable: 12/12 pairs, two runs). s6740: the
  port side was raw Display-P3 screencapture values; after P3->sRGB the hue-dependent part vanishes, leaving a uniform
  2.5% gain in the 512 flight only. Lesson: convert tagged captures before any colour comparison.


- s6458 "G3c(c) turning shake closed as retail 30 Hz judder" and s6455 "camera jerk identical in all arms" (s6696: every run
  since s6372 ran at ~17 game fps with bunched presents from our own per-vector-load getenv). Believable because the jerk
  was arm-independent: the overhead was in every arm, retail included.

### Superseded conclusions — do not act on these
- s6990 "60.0 fps on all 19 levels at 16:9" and s6962 "LEVEL=4 16:9 58.5, LEVEL=10 60.0" (superseded s6991): tools/g1e_owner_quiet_arms.zsh hardcoded ROGUESQ_FORCE_UNLOCK=1, which clamps the level-select cursor to level 1 whatever FORCE_SAVE_MISSION says; every arm logged cursorMask=0x2 (s6962 l4/l10 too), so all of them flew level 1. Believable because [saveslot] force=<lvl> printed the requested level in every log. The harness now sets FORCE_UNLOCK to the requested level and flags a cursorMask mismatch; the scorer prints the level actually flown (cur).
- s6991 "21:9 selects a 2000-slot texture-table layout" (superseded s6992): the 2000 count was read after the corruption; the fixed 21:9 run reads 2048. Believable because it differed by aspect in the same arm table.
- s6984 "VI->Q is not longer on lates" and s6986 "lates miss the latch by commit phase, so the guest VI phase must drift" (superseded s6987): the chain Q -> last W -> last kick before W picked the NEXT frame's kick on lates because their late W lands after it (kick->commit 5 ms < send_dl 10 ms gave it away). Believable because the normal-frame chain was right and the commit-phase histogram was real. Corrected chain: R->W (workload render) is the late term; VI phase is equal.
- s6968 "ROGUESQ_VI_LOCK=1 cuts 21:9 latency ~31 -> 23.4" read as the lock's effect alone (superseded s6969): k1-k3 had DRAIN_ACQ=8 armed; LOCK alone from boot sat at level 99% (lat 46) because the lock pauses at level. Believable because the before-blocks happened to have no level. The gain is LOCK+drain; VI_LOCK=1 now implies ACQ=8.
- s6967 "the 21:9 level still forms with RT via even-cadence onsets (r2 7/7) -> phase-lock VI to vsync because two free clocks drift" (superseded s6968): r2's level formed at the 59.0 s policy-toggle instant (Q gap 34 ms) and its 7 "onsets" were acq re-crossings of 5 ms inside that persisting level; VI-display drift is 2-8 ppm, too slow to trigger anything. Believable because the onset detector (10 low presents then acq>5) cannot tell a new level from a shallow level wobbling at the threshold. The phase still matters, but through the submit phase (s6968).
- **"Port 4:3 presentation has retail shape" (assumed through s6927; s6717 left the side bars unchecked).** Believable because every G3 match compared framebuffers or RDP, which do match. Retail VI spans 640 dots for 512 columns (s6928): the presented box was 20% narrow.
- s6926 "pillared 512 screens are ~14% narrow at wide aspect": superseded s6927. Title w/h 1.144, 1.140, 1.137. Believable because 0.64 of the window is true; the 0.75 reference was not, the 4:3 picture is itself 0.86 of its window.
- s6921-s6923 "noise block on the OPTIONS-to-TIE cut" and "reads like non-image memory" (settled s6924): the cut is into SHOWROOM, whose craft is random per run; the memory is live game data at an undrawn VI origin. Believable because the one craft seen in those runs was a TIE.
- s6921 "MELT alone paints a bright wedge on a lava shot, MELT must not become a default as it stands" and s6922 "no sky in the bubble frames, bright objects sit in a terrain gap" (superseded s6923): the bubble is the game's own mesh, present with MELT off and at retail settings. Believable because a toggle edge happened to land on a sweep of an animated object; a parity mean over 23 edges shows no effect. Sky is in 589 of 814 VIs.
- s6918 "H-select REFUTED, cutoff inputs match retail, so the cause is in the cell list" and H-order, H-dist, H-emit (superseded s6919): it sampled 0x8009DEB4 after the game's write, and our block overwrote it before the read. Believable because the values matched in every segment, moved with the scene, and had a working control. Sample at the reader. H-slip and H-input-camera refutations stand.
- s6917 NEXT "H-far-beam / H-ship: past-far objects or a retail distance cull" (superseded s6917): objects are submitted, the sky's moved depth hides them. Believable because FAR_TOG removes them too, by changing what is admitted.
- s6910 "floating dark triangles" as a far mesh or LOD, and NEXT H-mesh/H-lod (superseded s6911): they are single terrain quads with junk heights. Believable because they look like broken building pieces, and they sat beside real far buildings.
- s6791 G3f "camera slides 13 units in ~0.5 s while yaw lags ~3 s" and ITERATION G5g's wording of it (superseded s6907): those floats are the view translation, not position. World eye moves smoothly over ~3.8 s and yaw leads. Believable because the column sits where a position would, and retail shows the same curve. tools/g3f_pan_cmp.py reads the same column.
- s6895 "dd1 stays off: no benefit shown, owner calls dd1 clean" (superseded s6906): dd1 has the thickest knife lines, 29 vs 1 same run. Believable because the s6895 arm counted small transients on a quiet scene and the owner's "clean" was about terrain drops. Also G3c "CULL_SPIKE on" read as covering these: the cull only sees the RDP stream.

Believable because the logged x and z ranges look plainly wasteful.

Believable because three =tog arms agreed, each 30-40 s in the same early phase. Same-run toggles still need a whole flight on this level: use >=300 s for any rate claim.

### Run recipes and hard config

- Run from `build/` with the ROM beside it; SIGKILL to stop; one game run at a time.
- Current pinned dd4 lvl1 run: `zsh scratch/agent/s6549_run.sh <dd> <poolx>`. G5 arm template: `scratch/s6899/arm.zsh`; scenes: `scratch/s6908/arm.zsh` with EARLY_N=13 and FL_START past the scene (lvl5 needs >190).
- dd4 was enabled without `ROGUESQ_DD_UNSAFE` in s6582; higher exploratory settings use DD_UNSAFE (clamp 8). Confirm run.log echoes `multiplier N`.
- lvl10/15 need `ROGUESQ_FORCE_PLANET_UNLOCK=0xFF`. Wide soaks need `MISSION_WIDTH=796|1024` + `WIDE_ROUTE=1`; ASPECT implies `OSMEM_MB=12`.
- Pose control: `ROGUESQ_POSE_LOCK=1` (no input) + `ROGUESQ_POSE_FREEZE=<x,...>:<ms>` (needs RAND_TRACE + DEBUG_WRITE arm; `tools/g3_optin_pose_arms.sh`, PIN=1 pins dt). Dump ordinal is not a phase key.
- Pin dt: oracle RS64_XTRACE_POKE / port `ROGUESQ_XTRACE_POKE=800FA730:29:30:3d088889` (needs RAND_TRACE).
- Timing: any ROGUESQ_LOG_* env turns FAST off and PROBES on, so set `ROGUESQ_G1E_FAST=1 ROGUESQ_G1E_PROBES=0`. Log text itself has no measured cost (s6884). Per-frame meter: `[g1b]` lines in run.log (sd_wall, tasks/s).
- Present rings (ROGUESQ_PRESENT_RING=<file>): check tools/g1e_present_cadence.py first, latency figures are per display. A ring with at=0 throughout is NOT a measurement. A UG27 never gives reports. The game can open behind the owner's windows (s6891; it did not in s6931) and needs part of itself visible: ROGUESQ_WINDOW_POS=x,y, tools/g1e_display_free.swift. Read acq_ms on ungated rings only.
- Freeze measures: scratch/s6902/arm_m.zsh is the metered arm, no capture; stalls = [g1b] sd_wall max, image freezes = tools/g5c_frozen_runs.py on a g5b_capture .raw. g5b_drops gap figures cannot see a freeze (s6902). `sample <pid> <s> <ms>` on a live run costs no build.
- AT THE MOVIES shots by run time, dd1 16:9: 76 sea level 887-912, 77 fleet 912-924, 78 sea to city 924-942, 79 banked 942-952 (s6915). Pair arms by cam rows, dd4 trails 1-3 s. Pixel-free retail check: tools/g3_rdp_top_envelope.py.
- g5b_capture delay runs from window found, not launch: for a run-time target start it fresh with delay 0 (s6914). Frame comparison: window captures are Display-P3, convert to sRGB; `--dec shift` (v<<3); port RDRAM fb dumps lack RT64 3D frames, so use window captures. Score menus by RDP (tools/g3_rdp_frame_match.py, pair runner tools/g3_menu_pair.sh, retail offset 7.3 s), not pixels. Title decode: --w 512 --h 448 --bases 790000 --win 64,1024 --winx 85,1191.
- Oracle missions: tools/g3_eep_patch.py sets +0x31; bonus 18/19 need d-pad RIGHT on SELECT LEVEL; m17 race needs a one-shot rngSeed poke. Use --save-dir (g3_mission/run.sh), never swap a save over the user .eep. Do not re-run mission-3 flight.
- Soak verdicts: `scratch/agent/SOAK-RESULTS.md`; read `alive_at_end` / `crashlines`, never rc. A queued repeat soak is not a work unit.
- Full dd knob/instrument table: PROJECT-OVERVIEW "G1c draw-distance knob and recipe reference"; owner guide `docs/DRAW-DISTANCE.md`; owner commands `docs/OWNER-OPT-INS.md`.

### G1 mission coverage

Playable levels are 0..18 (`NUM_LEVELS=0x13`); 19/20 are sentinels. Route/hold coverage and framebuffer presence are distinct from objective response. Level 1 has a retail flight match. Level 0/1/2/3/4/5 named counter responses are observed; remaining objective response coverage is partial. No level is promoted here to fully VERIFIED. See [framebuffer coverage](G1-FRAMEBUFFER-COVERAGE.md) and [objective contracts, evidence and limits](G1-OBJECTIVE-RESPONSE.md). Mission wins, aim/steer and mission-to-mission progression remain owner playtest. Per-level counter contracts s6678-s6687: PROJECT-OVERVIEW.

### Durable constraints
- Runs longer than a turn: never end the turn to wait, the Stop gate counts it, and a background run can die with the session (s6865 arm B got SDL_QUIT 5 s before the iteration ended). Run in the foreground (Bash timeout up to 600 s) or queue a soak (s6866).
- Retail defaults remain unchanged. Opt-ins include draw distance, aspect, FPS60, spike culling, and audio control. Do not make an opt-in default from a single-source result.
- `ROGUESQ_DRAW_DISTANCE`: dd2 qualified lvl1/5/10; dd3/dd4/dd6 300 s holds clean lvl1/5/10 under DD_UNSAFE; dd8 lvl1/5 clean. Crash-free holds do not mean "renders correctly" (s6468: dd>=4 ground missing before the bypass). No mitigation is acceptable without naming the writer and establishing value legitimacy; dd>1 fixes live in `tools/apply_s6*.py` and fixup scripts.
- Wide rendering uses runtime RAM-top handling and a larger reported memory arm; default remains 4:3/retail. Wide-only hangar band (s6602) CLOSED s6840; native hangar geometry remains parked.
- New apply scripts go in RS64_REPLAY only, never as inline calls (docs/REGEN-VERIFY.md, s6881). Generated diagnostics must survive regeneration through fixup tooling. Never reset, clean, checkout, or update submodules. If editing `lib/`, run `./submodule-patches/export.sh` and commit the refreshed patches.
- Controls: get_n64_input is the pre-6ed036b97 mapping (owner had the PS4 remap and stick shaping reverted). Do not change controls without an owner request.
- The title plume is parked after clean boots. Reopen only on new evidence.
- Read `docs/F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md` before interpreting Factor 5 streams. Ground truth must precede new instrumentation; every null needs a positive control and two independent lines of evidence before changing this file.

#### Run recipes and hard config

- Run from `build/` with the ROM beside it; SIGKILL to stop; one game run at a time.
- Disk is ~20 GB free: a 960x540 g5b_capture is ~9 GB/min (s7002 filled the disk at 125 s). Keep captures <= 90 s, delete raws after scoring.
- Pinned dd4 lvl1 run: `zsh scratch/agent/s6549_run.sh <dd> <poolx>`. G5 arm template
  `scratch/s6899/arm.zsh`; scenes `scratch/s6908/arm.zsh` (EARLY_N=13, FL_START past the scene).
  Hangar camera arms: `scratch/s6907/arm.zsh`, log ROGUESQ_G5G_CAM=<file>, score tools/g5g_pan_score.py.
  Per-level owner-recipe fps: tools/g1e_owner_quiet_arms.zsh (sets FORCE_UNLOCK to the level; check `cur`).
- dd4 needs no DD_UNSAFE (s6582); higher uses DD_UNSAFE (clamp 8). Confirm run.log echoes `multiplier N`.
- lvl10/15 need `ROGUESQ_FORCE_PLANET_UNLOCK=0xFF`. L10 flight is cloud with no terrain grid (s7000). Wide soaks need `MISSION_WIDTH=796|1024` +
  `WIDE_ROUTE=1`; ASPECT implies `OSMEM_MB=12`.
- Pose control: `ROGUESQ_POSE_LOCK=1` + `ROGUESQ_POSE_FREEZE=<x,...>:<ms>` (needs RAND_TRACE +
  DEBUG_WRITE; tools/g3_optin_pose_arms.sh, PIN=1 pins dt). Port dt pin:
  `ROGUESQ_XTRACE_POKE=800FA730:29:30:3d088889` (oracle RS64_XTRACE_POKE).
- Timing: any ROGUESQ_LOG_* turns FAST off and PROBES on: set `ROGUESQ_G1E_FAST=1 ROGUESQ_G1E_PROBES=0`.
  Per-frame meter `[g1b]` (sd_wall, tasks/s).
- Present rings (ROGUESQ_PRESENT_RING): check tools/g1e_present_cadence.py first; at=0 throughout
  is not a measurement; the window must be partly visible (ROGUESQ_WINDOW_POS). Late-present
  positive control: load generator scratch/s6982/burst.
- g5b_capture is sRGB at source since s7151 (.cs sidecar). Raws captured before s7151 are Display-P3 untagged: score them with FID_P3=1.
- Freezes: stalls = [g1b] sd_wall max; image freezes = tools/g5c_frozen_runs.py on a g5b_capture
  .raw; `sample <pid> <s> <ms>` costs no build.
- AT THE MOVIES shots by run time (dd1 16:9): 76 887-912, 77 912-924, 78 924-942, 79 942-952 s.
- Frame comparison: window captures are Display-P3, convert to sRGB; port RDRAM fb dumps lack
  RT64 3D frames; score menus by RDP (tools/g3_rdp_frame_match.py, tools/g3_menu_pair.sh).
- Oracle missions: tools/g3_eep_patch.py sets +0x31; use --save-dir, never swap a save over the
  user .eep. Do not re-run mission-3 flight.
- Soak verdicts: `scratch/agent/SOAK-RESULTS.md`; read `alive_at_end` / `crashlines`, never rc.
- Knob tables: PROJECT-OVERVIEW "G1c draw-distance knob and recipe reference";
  docs/DRAW-DISTANCE.md; owner commands docs/OWNER-OPT-INS.md.

#### G1 mission coverage

Playable levels 0..18 (`NUM_LEVELS=0x13`); 19/20 are sentinels. All have route, 300 s holds and
framebuffer presence; level 1 has a retail flight match; objective response (d) parked by owner.
See docs/G1-FRAMEBUFFER-COVERAGE.md and docs/G1-OBJECTIVE-RESPONSE.md. Never send hull damage on
level 8 (counter3==1 fails the mission).

#### Durable constraints
- Never end a turn to wait on a run: foreground (timeout <= 600 s) or queue a soak (s6865/s6866).
- Retail defaults stay unless the owner chooses; never make an opt-in default from a single source.
- Crash-free holds do not mean "renders correctly" (s6468). No mitigation without naming the
  writer; dd>1 fixes live in `tools/apply_s6*.py` (registered in RS64_REPLAY only, docs/REGEN-VERIFY.md).
- Any guest pointer the game range-tests must sit where its test accepts it: 0x81000000+ fails
  `(p & 0xFF000000) == 0x80000000` unless ROGUESQ_PTRMASK (s6992). Re-check this for any new arena.
- Never reset, clean, checkout or update submodules; after editing `lib/` run
  `./submodule-patches/export.sh` and commit.
- Controls: get_n64_input is the pre-6ed036b97 mapping; no changes without an owner request.
- Title plume parked; reopen only on new evidence.
- Read `docs/F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md` before interpreting Factor 5 streams. Positive control for
  every null; two independent lines before a conclusion enters this file.

##### Run recipes and hard config

- Run from `build/` with the ROM beside it; SIGKILL to stop; one game run at a time.
- Disk is ~20 GB free: a 960x540 g5b_capture is ~9 GB/min (s7002 filled the disk at 125 s). Keep captures <= 90 s, delete raws after scoring.
- Pinned dd4 lvl1 run: `zsh scratch/agent/s6549_run.sh <dd> <poolx>`. G5 arm template
  `scratch/s6899/arm.zsh`; scenes `scratch/s6908/arm.zsh` (EARLY_N=13, FL_START past the scene).
  Hangar camera arms: `scratch/s6907/arm.zsh`, log ROGUESQ_G5G_CAM=<file>, score tools/g5g_pan_score.py.
  Per-level owner-recipe fps: tools/g1e_owner_quiet_arms.zsh (sets FORCE_UNLOCK to the level; check `cur`).
- dd4 needs no DD_UNSAFE (s6582); higher uses DD_UNSAFE (clamp 8). Confirm run.log echoes `multiplier N`.
- lvl10/15 need `ROGUESQ_FORCE_PLANET_UNLOCK=0xFF`. L10 flight is cloud with no terrain grid (s7000). Wide soaks need `MISSION_WIDTH=796|1024` +
  `WIDE_ROUTE=1`; ASPECT implies `OSMEM_MB=12`.
- Pose control: `ROGUESQ_POSE_LOCK=1` + `ROGUESQ_POSE_FREEZE=<x,...>:<ms>` (needs RAND_TRACE +
  DEBUG_WRITE; tools/g3_optin_pose_arms.sh, PIN=1 pins dt). Port dt pin:
  `ROGUESQ_XTRACE_POKE=800FA730:29:30:3d088889` (oracle RS64_XTRACE_POKE).
- Timing: any ROGUESQ_LOG_* turns FAST off and PROBES on: set `ROGUESQ_G1E_FAST=1 ROGUESQ_G1E_PROBES=0`.
  Per-frame meter `[g1b]` (sd_wall, tasks/s).
- Present rings (ROGUESQ_PRESENT_RING): check tools/g1e_present_cadence.py first; at=0 throughout
  is not a measurement; the window must be partly visible (ROGUESQ_WINDOW_POS). Late-present
  positive control: load generator scratch/s6982/burst.
- g5b_capture is sRGB at source since s7151 (.cs sidecar). Raws captured before s7151 are Display-P3 untagged: score them with FID_P3=1.
- Freezes: stalls = [g1b] sd_wall max; image freezes = tools/g5c_frozen_runs.py on a g5b_capture
  .raw; `sample <pid> <s> <ms>` costs no build.
- AT THE MOVIES shots by run time (dd1 16:9): 76 887-912, 77 912-924, 78 924-942, 79 942-952 s.
- Frame comparison: window captures are Display-P3, convert to sRGB; port RDRAM fb dumps lack
  RT64 3D frames; score menus by RDP (tools/g3_rdp_frame_match.py, tools/g3_menu_pair.sh).
- Oracle missions: tools/g3_eep_patch.py sets +0x31; use --save-dir, never swap a save over the
  user .eep. Do not re-run mission-3 flight.
- Soak verdicts: `scratch/agent/SOAK-RESULTS.md`; read `alive_at_end` / `crashlines`, never rc.
- Knob tables: PROJECT-OVERVIEW "G1c draw-distance knob and recipe reference";
  docs/DRAW-DISTANCE.md; owner commands docs/OWNER-OPT-INS.md.

##### Durable constraints
- Never end a turn to wait on a run: foreground (timeout <= 600 s) or queue a soak (s6865/s6866).
- Retail defaults stay unless the owner chooses; never make an opt-in default from a single source.
- Crash-free holds do not mean "renders correctly" (s6468). No mitigation without naming the
  writer; dd>1 fixes live in `tools/apply_s6*.py` (registered in RS64_REPLAY only, docs/REGEN-VERIFY.md).
- Any guest pointer the game range-tests must sit where its test accepts it: 0x81000000+ fails
  `(p & 0xFF000000) == 0x80000000` unless ROGUESQ_PTRMASK (s6992). Re-check this for any new arena.
- Never reset, clean, checkout or update submodules; after editing `lib/` run
  `./submodule-patches/export.sh` and commit.
- Controls: get_n64_input is the pre-6ed036b97 mapping; no changes without an owner request.
- Title plume parked; reopen only on new evidence.
- Read `docs/F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md` before interpreting Factor 5 streams. Positive control for
  every null; two independent lines before a conclusion enters this file.

### Run recipes and hard config

- Run from `build/` with the ROM beside it; SIGKILL to stop; one game run at a time.
- Disk ~20 GB free: a 960x540 g5b_capture is ~9 GB/min. Keep captures <= 90 s, delete raws after scoring.
- Arms: tools/g1e_owner_quiet_arms.zsh (per-level owner fps; sets FORCE_UNLOCK, check `cur`); G5 template
  `scratch/s6899/arm.zsh`; scenes `scratch/s6908/arm.zsh`; hangar `scratch/s6907/arm.zsh` + tools/g5g_pan_score.py;
  fog/edge sheets tools/s7306_fog_219.zsh, tools/s7263_widewin_edge_arms.zsh (SHEET=1), tools/s7268_edge_delta.py;
  image holds tools/s7272_g5c_hold_arm.zsh + s7272_image_hold.py; toggle load tools/s7277_toggle_load_arm.zsh.
- dd4 needs no DD_UNSAFE; higher uses DD_UNSAFE (clamp 8). Confirm run.log echoes `multiplier N`.
- lvl10/15 need `ROGUESQ_FORCE_PLANET_UNLOCK=0xFF`. L10 is cloud with no terrain grid: never use it for terrain
  measures. Wide soaks need `MISSION_WIDTH=796|1024` + `WIDE_ROUTE=1`; ASPECT implies `OSMEM_MB=12`. 16:9 autopilot
  gates wait on VI width 1592, not 1024 (s7271).
- Pose control (s7308: PIN=1 repeat arms are pixel-identical at a freeze, so cross-run arm diffs are exact there; score with
  tools/s7308_pose_horizon.py): `ROGUESQ_POSE_LOCK=1` + `ROGUESQ_POSE_FREEZE=<x,...>:<ms>` (needs RAND_TRACE + DEBUG_WRITE;
  tools/g3_optin_pose_arms.sh). Port dt pin `ROGUESQ_XTRACE_POKE=800FA730:29:30:3d088889`.
- Timing: any ROGUESQ_LOG_* turns FAST off and PROBES on: set `ROGUESQ_G1E_FAST=1 ROGUESQ_G1E_PROBES=0`, or
  OWNER_TIMING=1 in the harness. Per-frame meter `[g1b]` (sd_wall, tasks/s). Measure on AC power (battery x1.4).
- Present rings (ROGUESQ_PRESENT_RING): tools/g1e_present_cadence.py first; at=0 throughout is not a measurement.
- g5b_capture is sRGB since s7151; raws before s7151 are Display-P3 (FID_P3=1).
- Freezes: stalls = [g1b] sd_wall max; image freezes = tools/g5c_frozen_runs.py / s7272_image_hold.py;
  `sample <pid> <s> <ms>` costs no build.
- AT THE MOVIES shots by run time (dd1 16:9): 76 887-912, 77 912-924, 78 924-942, 79 942-952 s.
- Frame comparison: score menus by RDP (tools/g3_rdp_frame_match.py, tools/g3_menu_pair.sh). G3 kit: arms
  tools/s7125_arm.zsh, s7131_arm.zsh, s7141_{arm,post}.zsh, s7146_arm.zsh, post s7152_post.zsh; scorers
  tools/s7122_fidelity.py (FID_ALROWS=444/336: RT64 shows rows 0-443 / 0-335), s7183_native_edge.py,
  s7210_regfit.py (run first at 16:9); replay tools/angrylion_replay/build16.sh. L17 autopilot dies ~126 s.
- Oracle missions: tools/g3_eep_patch.py sets +0x31; use --save-dir, never swap a save over the user .eep.
- Soak verdicts: `scratch/agent/SOAK-RESULTS.md`; read `alive_at_end` / `crashlines`, never rc. Recipes that

### Durable constraints
- Never end a turn to wait on a run: foreground (timeout <= 600 s) or queue a soak.
- Retail defaults stay unless the owner chooses; never make an opt-in default from a single source.
- Crash-free holds do not mean "renders correctly" (s6468). No mitigation without naming the writer; dd>1 fixes
  live in `tools/apply_s6*.py` (registered in RS64_REPLAY only, docs/REGEN-VERIFY.md).
- The RSP DMA keeps bit 24 (s7327, phys < 32 MB); RDP image addresses and the game's own 24-bit rebuilds (class D) still drop it, so
  textures / colour images / DL-pool refs must stay below 0x81000000.
- Any guest pointer the game range-tests must sit where its test accepts it: 0x81000000+ fails
  `(p & 0xFF000000) == 0x80000000` unless ROGUESQ_PTRMASK (s6992). Re-check for any new arena.
- Never reset, clean, checkout or update submodules; after editing `lib/` run `./submodule-patches/export.sh` and commit.
- Controls: get_n64_input is the pre-6ed036b97 mapping; no changes without an owner request.
- Title plume parked; reopen only on new evidence.
- Read `docs/F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md` before interpreting Factor 5 streams. Positive control for every null; two
  independent lines before a conclusion enters this file.

### Run recipes and hard config

- Run from `build/` with the ROM beside it; SIGKILL to stop; one game run at a time.
- Disk ~20 GB free: a 960x540 g5b_capture is ~9 GB/min. Keep captures <= 90 s, delete raws after scoring.
- Arms: tools/g1e_owner_quiet_arms.zsh (per-level owner fps; sets FORCE_UNLOCK, check `cur`); G5 template
  `scratch/s6899/arm.zsh`; scenes `scratch/s6908/arm.zsh`; hangar `scratch/s6907/arm.zsh` + tools/g5g_pan_score.py;
  fog/edge sheets tools/s7306_fog_219.zsh, tools/s7263_widewin_edge_arms.zsh (SHEET=1), tools/s7268_edge_delta.py;
  image holds tools/s7272_g5c_hold_arm.zsh + s7272_image_hold.py; toggle load tools/s7277_toggle_load_arm.zsh.
- dd4 needs no DD_UNSAFE; higher uses DD_UNSAFE (clamp 8). Confirm run.log echoes `multiplier N`.
- lvl10/15 need `ROGUESQ_FORCE_PLANET_UNLOCK=0xFF`. L10 is cloud with no terrain grid: never use it for terrain
  measures. Wide soaks need `MISSION_WIDTH=796|1024` + `WIDE_ROUTE=1`; ASPECT implies `OSMEM_MB=12`. 16:9 autopilot
  gates wait on VI width 1592, not 1024 (s7271).
- Pose control (s7308: PIN=1 repeat arms are pixel-identical at a freeze, so cross-run arm diffs are exact there; score with
  tools/s7308_pose_horizon.py): `ROGUESQ_POSE_LOCK=1` + `ROGUESQ_POSE_FREEZE=<x,...>:<ms>` (needs RAND_TRACE + DEBUG_WRITE;
  tools/g3_optin_pose_arms.sh). Port dt pin `ROGUESQ_XTRACE_POKE=800FA730:29:30:3d088889`.
- Timing: any ROGUESQ_LOG_* turns FAST off and PROBES on: set `ROGUESQ_G1E_FAST=1 ROGUESQ_G1E_PROBES=0`, or
  OWNER_TIMING=1 in the harness. Per-frame meter `[g1b]` (sd_wall, tasks/s). Measure on AC power (battery x1.4).
- Present rings (ROGUESQ_PRESENT_RING): tools/g1e_present_cadence.py first; at=0 throughout is not a measurement.
- g5b_capture is sRGB since s7151; raws before s7151 are Display-P3 (FID_P3=1).
- Freezes: stalls = [g1b] sd_wall max; image freezes = tools/g5c_frozen_runs.py / s7272_image_hold.py;
  `sample <pid> <s> <ms>` costs no build.
- AT THE MOVIES shots by run time (dd1 16:9): 76 887-912, 77 912-924, 78 924-942, 79 942-952 s.
- Frame comparison: score menus by RDP (tools/g3_rdp_frame_match.py, tools/g3_menu_pair.sh). G3 kit: arms
  tools/s7125_arm.zsh, s7131_arm.zsh, s7141_{arm,post}.zsh, s7146_arm.zsh, post s7152_post.zsh; scorers
  tools/s7122_fidelity.py (FID_ALROWS=444/336: RT64 shows rows 0-443 / 0-335), s7183_native_edge.py,
  s7210_regfit.py (run first at 16:9); replay tools/angrylion_replay/build16.sh. L17 autopilot dies ~126 s.
- Oracle missions: tools/g3_eep_patch.py sets +0x31; use --save-dir, never swap a save over the user .eep.
- Slow builds (TSan/ASan): `ROGUESQ_AUTOPILOT_CLOCK=frames ROGUESQ_AUTOPILOT_FPS=58` (FPS60) keys autopilot to fullsyncs,
  but front-end screens are VI-timed, so the route still diverges at TSan speed; gate with `<s>:w<width>` events (s7371).
- Soak verdicts: `scratch/agent/SOAK-RESULTS.md`; read `alive_at_end` / `crashlines`, never rc. Recipes that
  drive the window carry `# SOAK_NEEDS_IDLE=<secs>`; zsh recipes run under their shebang shell (s7287).
- Knob tables: PROJECT-OVERVIEW "G1c draw-distance knob and recipe reference"; docs/DRAW-DISTANCE.md;
  owner commands docs/OWNER-OPT-INS.md.

### G1 mission coverage

Playable levels 0..18 (`NUM_LEVELS=0x13`); 19/20 are sentinels. All have route, 300 s holds and framebuffer
presence; level 1 has a retail flight match; objective response (d) parked by owner. See
docs/G1-FRAMEBUFFER-COVERAGE.md and docs/G1-OBJECTIVE-RESPONSE.md. Never send hull damage on level 8.

### Durable constraints
- Never end a turn to wait on a run: foreground (timeout <= 600 s) or queue a soak.
- Retail defaults stay unless the owner chooses; never make an opt-in default from a single source.
- Crash-free holds do not mean "renders correctly" (s6468). No mitigation without naming the writer; dd>1 fixes
  live in `tools/apply_s6*.py` (registered in RS64_REPLAY only, docs/REGEN-VERIFY.md).
- The RSP DMA keeps bit 24 (s7327, phys < 32 MB); RDP image addresses and the game's own 24-bit rebuilds (class D) still drop it, so
  textures / colour images / DL-pool refs must stay below 0x81000000.
- Any guest pointer the game range-tests must sit where its test accepts it: 0x81000000+ fails
  `(p & 0xFF000000) == 0x80000000` unless ROGUESQ_PTRMASK (s6992). Re-check for any new arena.
- Never reset, clean, checkout or update submodules; after editing `lib/` run `./submodule-patches/export.sh` and commit.
- Controls: get_n64_input is the pre-6ed036b97 mapping; no changes without an owner request.
- Title plume parked; reopen only on new evidence.
- Read `docs/F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md` before interpreting Factor 5 streams. Positive control for every null; two
  independent lines before a conclusion enters this file.

## Default-on internal guards and fixes (s7720 table; source of truth `tools/s7557_gq_census.py --strict`)
These settings are ON when unset. `=0` turns each off (restores the old behaviour); they are not owner opt-ins and must
not be flipped without the owner. Every row was read from the getenv site in s7720.
| Setting | Session | Where | What it does when on (default) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ROGUESQ_AUDIO_PRIVATE_DMEM` | s4250 | librecomp rsp.cpp | audio LLE tasks run on a private DMEM copy, so no shared-DMEM lock with gfx |
| `ROGUESQ_AUDIO_WAIT_NOPUMP` | s327/s4192 | generated funcs (fixup_game_funcs_vendored.py) | unset = mode 2: the A12 countdown wait yields to the real producer; `0` = old musyxSynthFrame pump, `1` = blind spin (deadlocks) |
| `ROGUESQ_COPY_GUARD` | s5037 | upstream_compat.cpp | skips a guest memcpy whose src/dst leaves guest RAM (M3 idiom guard) |
| `ROGUESQ_DD_OFFMAPCULL_EYE` | s7032 | upstream_compat.cpp | dd>1 off-map cull keyed on the eye position (inert at dd1) |
| `ROGUESQ_DPC_KEEP_PIPE` | s4272 | dpc_bridge.cpp | keeps pending pipe-sync state across deferred DPC submits |
| `ROGUESQ_DPC_WRAP_FLUSH` | s4273/s4549 | dpc_bridge.cpp | on a DPC ring wrap, flushes pending ranges to RT64 before restarting the ring mark (lap-1 commands not lost) |
| `ROGUESQ_FL_HDR_HARD_SKIP` | s4548/s659 | rt64 rt64_framebuffer.cpp / rt64_state.cpp | skips RT64 framebuffer writeback over a guest freelist header range |
| `ROGUESQ_G1D_FPDEPTH` | s6879 | generated funcs (apply_s6879_fpdepth.py) | scales the 0x8004395C far-plane depth store by the draw-distance factor (identity at dd1) |
| `ROGUESQ_G1D_OVL_WRAP` | s6848 | main.cpp (apply_s6848_ovlwrap.py) | wide-view overlay coordinate wrap fix (inert at 4:3) |
| `ROGUESQ_HLE_PATCH_ALPHA` | upstream RT64 HLE | rt64 rt64_gbi_f3dfactor5.cpp | HLE-path all-7s alpha combiner rewrite to alpha=1 (HLE only; this port runs the gfx ucode LLE) |
| `ROGUESQ_PIO_GUARD` | s5062 | librecomp pi.cpp | skips a 4-byte PIO read whose ROM span leaves the cart or whose RDRAM dest leaves RAM |
| `ROGUESQ_PI_DMA_GUARD` | s5061 | librecomp pi.cpp | skips an out-of-range PI DMA but still posts its completion message |
| `ROGUESQ_PI_UNK_COMPLETE` | s7196 | librecomp pi.cpp | a PI DMA to an unknown region still posts its completion message (no guest hang) |
| `ROGUESQ_PREEMPT_POINT` | s6808 | ultramodern mesgqueue.cpp | guest preemption point when a host message is pending |
| `ROGUESQ_S4272` | s4272/s4549 | dpc_bridge.cpp | deferred-submit shadow path of the DPC bridge |
| `ROGUESQ_S6892` | s6892/s7571 | upstream_compat.cpp | G5a cinematic spline walker pointer repair (logs to build/rs64_s6892.log) |
| `ROGUESQ_S7685_POSSUB` | s7685 | rs64_standins.cpp | stand-ins reject a position match whose caller is a different known subtype (only with STANDINS) |
| `ROGUESQ_SPAI_GUARD` | s5063 | librecomp sp.cpp | skips an SP/AI DMA whose span leaves guest RAM |
| `ROGUESQ_WRAP_RESTORE` | s4287 | dpc_bridge.cpp | restores the pre-wrap DPC range after a ring wrap |
`ROGUESQ_S7593_QUIT_AFTER` / `ROGUESQ_S7593_QUIT_ON_GAP_MS` are soak-harness quit timers (gap quit is off by default, -1);
they change no game state and are classified diag in the census.
